questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up so you can turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is about to end. If you are turning in the direction of the arrow, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn around and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror regularly to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is joining ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is joining ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that a side road will intersect ahead. Be alert and ready.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Assume the child has full control of the bicycle.
Be ready for anything unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for anything unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable. Young riders often make sudden direction changes. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see, so expect the unexpected.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver can pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas in your vision when you get tired.
Areas you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas you cannot see in your vehicle's mirrors.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to go. Check the rear corners of your vehicle. These hidden areas are called blind spots because mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: When passing another car, when do you have enough space to return to the driving lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to re-enter the lane.
When you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to the driving lane, make sure there is a safe gap between your vehicle and the one you just passed. When you see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You should stop for other traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Give space so drivers can merge safely into traffic.
Traffic is entering from another road. Stay in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is entering from another road. Give space so drivers can merge safely into traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic will merge into your road. Check your mirrors and move to another lane if possible to help merging drivers have a clear path.

questions.question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can clearly see both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Once the gate is up, only cross if you can clearly see in both directions and no trains are coming.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Passing is not safe in this area.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not safe in this area.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass in that area. It is illegal and unsafe to pass where you see this sign because visibility is limited.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Expect them to drive above the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks with flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings. Be ready to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway.
Railroad warning.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting ahead.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before you enter a curve. You may not see hazards ahead. Braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars:

options.text: Cannot be seen or are so close that they prevent the truck driver from stopping and turning safely.
Have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be seen or are so close that they prevent the truck driver from stopping and turning safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks and buses where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where cars are too close to allow the truck or bus driver to stop and turn safely. A car in a "No zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Your reaction time gets slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It also reduces how well you can see and makes you less alert. As you drink more alcohol, your judgment gets worse and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances, speeds, and other vehicles.

questions.question: You may pass a vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means drivers can cross from either lane. A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass from the lane with the broken line, but not from the lane with the solid line. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and lights on. You should:

options.text: Stop right away in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren, finish crossing and then drive to the right and stop. You must give the right-of-way to any police car, fire truck, ambulance, or other emergency vehicle using lights or a siren.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower your blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating foods high in fat
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body.

questions.question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the left.
Passing is allowed from the right.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep your speed steady.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions ahead. This sign tells you that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: When you see someone crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
Honk your horn as you proceed past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the person is blind. You must stop and let them cross safely. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: A bad suspension can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Slack in the steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot over bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane as much as possible because the motorcycle is small and doesn't use all of the lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder so that you can pass.
Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane when passing. Never share the same lane with a motorcycle. If you return to your lane too soon, the rider may have to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left and right for vehicles or pedestrians. Look left a second time because cars coming from your left will be closer to you. Look across the whole intersection before moving to make sure it is clear.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.
Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. Drive to the right edge and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through first and then stop.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Do not stop when entering an interstate. Use the merging lane to speed up and smoothly blend with the fast-moving traffic already on the interstate.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Activate your turn signal.
Reduce your speed.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the speed limit for safety, but never faster. Reduce speed for curves, hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Slightly increase your speed.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unpredictable conditions. Drive with extra care to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: With oncoming vehicles on your left and parked vehicles on your right, steer down the middle between them.
